finalAnswerBlocks.value: Triangle W has vertices (0, 1), (3, 1) and (2, 2) — triangle X halved in size about the origin, with each side half the length of the corresponding side of X.

whyThisWorks.value: An enlargement with centre the origin scales the position vector of every point, so the coordinates are simply multiplied by the scale factor. A factor between 0 and 1 still counts as an enlargement in mathematics even though the image is smaller; the shape stays similar to the object, with all angles unchanged and all lengths in the ratio 1 : 2.
